hints: Focus on what each test is really telling you, one test for oxidation and one test for a specific group.
Decolourising warm acidified manganate(VII) means the alcohol can be oxidised, so rule out any tertiary alcohol first.
A yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine means a positive iodoform test, so look for the alcohol that contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit.
walkthrough:
**Use the manganate(VII) result**

Warm acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is a strong oxidising agent. It is decolourised by primary and secondary alcohols, but not by tertiary alcohols.

Rule: primary $\rightarrow$ aldehyde $\rightarrow$ acid, secondary $\rightarrow$ ketone, tertiary $\rightarrow$ no reaction

**Use the iodine result**

Alkaline aqueous iodine giving a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ is the iodoform test. For an alcohol, it is positive only if the molecule contains the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

Test group:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- + \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow s)}$$

**Check the four alcohols**

We need a secondary (or primary) alcohol that also has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

$\text{3-methylbutan-2-ol}$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. It is secondary so it is oxidised, and it clearly contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ so it gives iodoform. This fits both observations.

options.A: 2-methylbutan-2-ol is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a tertiary alcohol. It cannot be oxidised so it will not decolourise warm acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$, and it lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group so it is iodoform negative.
options.B: 3-methylbutan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, a secondary alcohol. It is oxidised to a ketone so it decolourises $\text{KMnO}_4$, and it contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ so it gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline iodine. It satisfies both tests.
options.C: Pentan-1-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, a primary alcohol. It does decolourise $\text{KMnO}_4$, but it has a $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it is iodoform negative.
options.D: Pentan-3-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a secondary alcohol. It does decolourise $\text{KMnO}_4$, but the group next to the $\text{C-OH}$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$, not $\text{CH}_3-$, so it does not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ and is iodoform negative.
